name: ISO 26262, road vehicles: functional safety
note: A starter set at the level of the standard's clauses, for software and the processes around it (parts 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8). The wording is our own short paraphrase of what each clause is for, never the standard's text. The part-and-clause numbers come from public descriptions of the 2018 edition: check each against your licensed copy before relying on it, and edit or delete what does not fit your product. Hardware (part 5) is left out.

clauses.title: Overall safety management
clauses.text: A safety culture, a safety organisation and a safety plan exist for the item.

clauses.title: Safety management during the concept phase and product development
clauses.text: Safety activities are planned, carried out, tracked and confirmed (reviews, audits, assessment) from concept to release.

clauses.title: Safety management after release for production
clauses.text: Responsibility for functional safety after release is assigned, and field experience is monitored and acted on.

clauses.title: Item definition
clauses.text: The item, its functions, boundaries, interfaces and operating environment are defined well enough to analyse.

clauses.title: Hazard analysis and risk assessment
clauses.text: Hazards are identified and rated, and safety goals with their integrity levels are set.

clauses.title: Functional safety concept
clauses.text: Each safety goal is refined into functional safety requirements and allocated to elements of the item.

clauses.title: Technical safety concept
clauses.text: Functional safety requirements are refined into technical safety requirements that can be designed and verified.

clauses.title: System architectural design
clauses.text: The system architecture implements the technical safety concept, and its elements carry the allocated safety requirements.

clauses.title: System and item integration and testing
clauses.text: Integrated elements are tested against the technical safety requirements, and the results are recorded.

clauses.title: Safety validation
clauses.text: The item is shown, in its intended use, to meet its safety goals.

clauses.title: Specification of software safety requirements
clauses.text: Software safety requirements are derived from the technical safety requirements, are unambiguous and verifiable, and trace to their source.

clauses.title: Software architectural design
clauses.text: The software architecture realises the software safety requirements, with its elements, interfaces and resource use described and checked.

clauses.title: Software unit design and implementation
clauses.text: Each software unit is designed and implemented to its requirements under the rules the safety level calls for.

clauses.title: Software unit verification
clauses.text: Software units are verified against their design and requirements, by review, analysis and test, and coverage is measured.

clauses.title: Software integration and verification
clauses.text: Software units are integrated step by step and the integrated software is verified against the architecture and its safety requirements.

clauses.title: Testing of the embedded software
clauses.text: The software is tested on target-representative hardware against the software safety requirements.

clauses.title: Interfaces within distributed developments
clauses.text: Where work is shared between organisations, each party's safety responsibilities and the evidence exchanged are agreed and recorded.

clauses.title: Specification and management of safety requirements
clauses.text: Safety requirements are written clearly, are consistent, are traced to their sources and to what satisfies them, and their changes are managed.

clauses.title: Configuration management
clauses.text: Work products are identified, versioned and baselined, and what was delivered can be reconstructed.

clauses.title: Change management
clauses.text: Changes to safety-related work products are requested, impact-analysed, approved and tracked.

clauses.title: Verification
clauses.text: Work products are verified against their inputs by planned, specified and recorded reviews, analyses and tests.

clauses.title: Documentation management
clauses.text: Safety-related documents are controlled: identified, reviewed, approved, kept and retrievable.

clauses.title: Confidence in the use of software tools
clauses.text: Tools whose failure could introduce or hide a fault are assessed, and the confidence placed in them is justified.

clauses.title: Qualification of software components
clauses.text: A software component reused from elsewhere is shown to be suitable for the safety requirements it is used for.
